title: Token pipeline load exercise and p95 drift alarms
creator: Avery Chen
description: Build and maintain a stable, reproducible microbenchmark harness that exercises the token pipeline for our core serving models and provides automated drift/regression alarms based on tokens-per-second and p95 latency signals. This ticket covers: the harness code, CI job integration, standard input corpora, variance-reduction techniques, alerting thresholds, dashboards, and on-call playbook entries. The goal is to detect regressions early (nightly CI and post-deploy canaries) and provide actionable diffs for engineering owners.
goals: Establish a reproducible load harness that measures steady-state tokens/sec and p95 latency for each core model variant
Integrate the harness into CI to run nightly baselines and on-demand PR probes
Implement an automated regression detector with configurable thresholds and Slack/Oncall alerts
Provide dashboards with historical baselines, CIs, and per-model variance so engineers can triage quickly
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run end-to-end in CI and complete for 3 core models within 30 minutes
Nightly job stores results in perf-store and populates the runtime-performance dashboard
Regression detector fires when tokens/sec drops by >6% (median) OR p95 increases by >10ms with >95% confidence
PRs that change runtime code automatically trigger the harness and post a summary comment with links and a green/red verdict
technical_approach: Synthetic driver that replays representative prompt mix with configurable sequence length distribution (short/med/long) and temperature settings
Warm-up phase to populate KV cache and reach steady-state before measurement window
Batching simulator to exercise real request batching shapes and measure per-token throughput
Statistical aggregation: run N=30 short-sweeps and report median + 95% bootstrap CI to reduce flakiness
Environment matrix: run on standard host types (a100-40g, a100-80g, g5/4) and quantization profiles where applicable
Persist raw traces to perf-store with tags: model, commit, kernel-set, region, env, seed
implementation_tasks: Create harness repo module (bench/engine) and interface with existing serving API
Add CI pipeline: .github/workflows/bench.yml to run nightly and on PR labels
Write canonical prompt corpus (bench/resources/prompt_corpus_v1.jsonl) and seed generator
Implement regression-detector lambda that compares latest run to rolling baseline and posts alerts
Wire perf-store ingestion and update Grafana dashboard panels
Document runbook and add example triage steps to oncall handbook
risks_and_tradeoffs: Cost: running full matrix nightly is expensive — mitigate by sampling a subset of models per night and full sweep weekly
Noise: infra variability can produce false positives — mitigated via N-run aggregation and confidence intervals
Coverage vs speed: shorter runs reduce cost but increase variance; acceptance criteria balance time (<=30m) vs stability
False negatives on rare regressions that only manifest under specific batching shapes — we include simulated batching matrix to reduce this

notes: Prefer harness code in TypeScript/Node to reuse existing SDK bindings; core sampling loops implemented in Rust if latency-critical. We will experiment with 15 vs 30-run sweeps in the first week and lock on the configuration that yields <3% CV for tokens/sec.
